title: Sortable
summary: Drag-and-drop list primitive for reordering, moving between lists and copying from a library by mouse, pen, touch and keyboard, with an optional insertion point that opens a searchable inserter; reports intent only.

preview.description: How a pointer drag shows where the item lands: silhouette lifts the item out of the list and opens an outline of its size at the place it would take, the list making room; line draws a thin line there and leaves the list as it is. Keyboard moves and external targets always use the line; a list that wraps into a grid opens the outline as one of its cells, in reading order.

inserter-items.description: Opt-in insertion point. JSON array (or the inserterItems property) of [{value, label, icon?, caption?, keywords?, disabled?}], with {type: "heading", label} and {type: "separator"} to group them. When it holds at least one item, a "+" on the gap between items (and before the first, after the last) opens a searchable inserter of these kinds; empty or absent, the list draws and does nothing more than before.

item_contract.description: Descendants with data-sf-sortable-item="<id>" are items; an optional data-sf-sortable-handle inside an item limits dragging to the handle and is the touch target.

drop_targets.description: SF.Sortable.registerSortableDropTarget({resolve, keyboardTargets, drop, leave}) joins non-list targets such as sf-composition-overlay to the same drag session; the session is shared across Smart bundles. Once loaded, SF.Sortable exposes SORTABLE_INTENT_EVENT, SORTABLE_STATE_EVENT, activeSortableSession, registerSortableDropTarget and sortableIndexAt.

inserter.description: The insertion point is one native icon button (size 1/3), the list's last tab stop, placed on the gap a pointer is near, after a focused row, or where its arrow keys put it. It opens sf-context-menu (openFor, local search over label, caption and keywords) anchored to the point. The component never creates the inserted item: it raises sf-sortable-insert and the host adds the item. Escape closes only the inserter, the innermost open surface (core open-surface-mark). Once loaded, SF.Sortable exposes SORTABLE_INSERT_EVENT.

sf-sortable-intent.summary: The person dropped an item; the host applies or refuses the change.

sf-sortable-state.summary: A drag session started (picked) or ended (dropped, cancelled).

sf-sortable-insert.summary: The person chose a kind in the inserter for a place in the list; the host creates the item at index. Bubbles, is composed and is cancelable: preventDefault() refuses and keeps the inserter open.

accessibility.focus: Items become focusable and describe the instructions. Space or Enter picks up, arrows move within a list and to other accepting lists or external targets, Space or Enter drops, Escape or Tab cancels. Every step is announced in a polite live region in the page language. With inserter items, + on a focused row opens the inserter for the place after it, and the insertion point is the list's last tab stop: arrows move it between places, Home and End go to the first and the last, Enter or Space opens the inserter; in the inserter typing filters, arrows and Enter choose, Escape closes it and returns focus.

ai_guidance.use_when: Use sf-sortable when people reorder or move host items, or drag library entries onto an editor canvas. Apply sf-sortable-intent to the host model with an expected revision; a refusal leaves the page unchanged. Give inserter-items when people insert new items at a place in the list; create the item on sf-sortable-insert.
do_not: Do not copy generated ui-smart code
Do not let the component move host DOM or save data
Do not rely on pointer dragging alone; keep the keyboard path
Do not bundle a private drag session; use SF.Sortable.registerSortableDropTarget
Do not let the component create the inserted item; add it on sf-sortable-insert
